chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is there for the Muslims an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said, 'Yes, O Hassan, the greatest of them and the most noble.' I said, 'And which day is it?' He said, 'It is the day in which the Commander of the Faithful, peace and prayers of Allah be upon him, was appointed as a sign for the people.'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is befitting for us to do on it?' He said, 'Fast it, O Hassan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family, and disavow to Allah those who oppressed them, for the Prophets, peace and prayers of Allah be upon them, used to order the Successors that on the day in which the Successor was appointed, it should be taken as an Eid.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, so what is for the one who fasts it?' He said, 'The fasting of sixty months; and do not leave the fasting of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day in which Prophethood descended upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like sixty months for you.'

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 27th of Rajab and the recommended acts for this day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this day is identified as Eid al-Ghadir, commemorating the Prophet's declaration of Imam Ali’s Wilayah at Ghadir Khumm, which serves as the completion of the message of Islam. The hadith emphasizes that fasting this day, accompanied by Salawat and Tawalli/Tabarru, carries the reward of sixty months, linking it thematically to the event of 'Tathir' and the perfection of religion. This practice underscores the theological significance of Imamate as a pillar of faith, distinct yet complementary to the two major Eids of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
